---
name: "MyOS Kernel Engineer"
description: "Use when changing or debugging MyOS's 32-bit x86 boot path, kernel, memory management, interrupts, Ring 3, hardware drivers, or QEMU tests."
tools: [read, search, edit, execute, todo]
user-invocable: true
---

You maintain MyOS, a freestanding 32-bit x86 kernel that boots through GRUB/Multiboot. Work from repository evidence, preserve the current architecture, and validate changes with the narrowest useful build or test.

## Repository map

- `Makefile`: compiler/tool selection, object rules, kernel/ISO builds, QEMU run targets, tests, and cleanup (`make clean` removes Python caches under `test/`). `make disk` creates a FAT32 `disk.img`; `make run` boots the GRUB ISO first and attaches an existing `$(DISK)` as a data disk, but does not create one. `make run-disk` creates the image if needed and boots with it attached. `make test` runs host-only Python `unittest`; test scripts must use host `cc` directly, never the kernel cross-compiler selected by `CC`. `make test-qemu` requires QEMU and `mkfs.fat`, assembles the ELF disk demo with NASM, and runs the bounded headless integration suite.
- `.gitignore`: generated build/image outputs and local editor/debug files.
- `linker.ld`: 1 MiB physical load, user-code placement, high-half kernel sections, and reserved paging storage.
- PAE uses 64-bit page-table entries and a 32-byte PDPT/32-bit CR3 while the CPU remains 32-bit. The PMM supports addresses below 64 GiB (36-bit PAE ceiling); use the single-slot kernel mapping window to access high frames/page tables, and honor the Multiboot memory map rather than assuming RAM exists up to the ceiling. For Multiboot v1, `mmap_length` is info dword 11 (offset 44) and `mmap_addr` is dword 12 (offset 48). The current bootstrap identity-maps only the first 16 MiB, so Multiboot info/map buffers must reside there. `make test-qemu-highmem` boots a separate GRUB ISO with QEMU TCG `-m 6G`, allocates a physical frame at or above 4 GiB, maps it, verifies write/read data, and frees/reallocates it; the standard integration suite remains at 128 MiB.
- `LICENSE`: project GPLv2 license.
- `TODO.md` and `TODO-zh.md`: English and Chinese project roadmaps. Keep their items and completion checkboxes synchronized; update both whenever a task changes or is completed.
- `boot/boot.asm`: Multiboot header, early page tables, initial stack, paging enable, and `kmain` entry.
- `boot/gdt.asm`, `boot/paging.asm`: assembly helpers for loading the GDT and enabling paging.
- `boot/interrupt.asm`: exception/IRQ/syscall stubs and the IRQ0 register-frame contract. The `isr14` stub also switches to a kernel `irq_frame` returned by `isr14_handler` when a faulting Ring 3 process is terminated, and the `syscall` stub does the same when `syscall_exit_frame` is set by `PROC_EXIT` (reusing the `irq0_resume` epilogue). The `int 0x80` gate is a DPL=3 trap gate (`0xEF`) so blocking syscalls can be woken by IRQ1.
- `src/arch/x86/trap.c`: `isr14_handler` demand-maps only registered user ranges (live-process ELF image ranges, 32 KiB user stacks at `0x810000`/`0x820000`, and the `USER_HEAP_*` range), zeroes new pages, kills the faulting process on illegal user access or protection violations, and panics on illegal kernel faults. It returns 0 for a normal `iret`, or a kernel `struct irq_frame *` to resume the shell context.
- `boot/user.asm`, `boot/elf_demo.asm`: Ring 3 demo and embedded ELF32 demo image (installs a `SIGINT` handler that prints `Bye` and exits; the same image is the `demo.elf` file on the QEMU test disk).
- `src/kernel.c`: keep the kernel entry and top-level initialization here.
- `src/arch/x86/`: x86 descriptor tables, interrupt/trap handlers, TSS, and port I/O.
- `src/mm/`: physical frames, virtual mappings/TLB, and kernel heap allocation.
- `src/os/`: panic handling, ELF loading, Ring 3 processes, system calls, and the signal mechanism (`ring3.c` owns per-process `sig_pending`/`sig_blocked`/`sig_handler[]`/`sig_active`/`sig_saved_frame`; numbers live in `include/os/signal.h` — only `SIGINT`=2 and `SIGKILL`=9 are implemented, others reserved; `SIG_VALID` gates send/handler).
- `src/shell/`: interactive shell (`shell.c`) with its public header in `include/shell/`.
- `docs/`: hand-written bilingual documentation split by language — `docs/en/` and `docs/zh/` mirror each other. `architecture.md` is the numbered-series index; `01-boot.md` through `14-mini-libc.md` cover boot, memory, interrupts, the syscall ABI (`04-syscall-abi.md`), Ring 3 processes, the shell (`07-shell.md`), the shell command table (`08-shell-commands.md`), FAT32 (`09-filesystem.md`), drivers (`10-drivers.md` plus the `12-driver-gaps.md` inventory/gap list), build/test, the driver gap analysis, signals (`13-signals.md`), and the `mini-libc/` user-space C library (`14-mini-libc.md`). **Whenever the syscall ABI or shell commands/behavior change, update `04-syscall-abi.md` and `08-shell-commands.md` (both languages) in the same change.** More generally, **every functional change must keep `docs/en/` and `docs/zh/` synchronized** — update the relevant numbered document(s) in both languages whenever behavior, commands, limits, or architecture details change.
- `src/drivers/`: ATA PIO, keyboard, PIC/PIT, TSC (`tsc.c` — calibrated against PIT after `sti`; 64-bit division is a hand-rolled shift loop because libgcc is unavailable), RTC, serial, VGA/VBE, ACPI, and font data. The RTC is treated as UTC and converted to Beijing time; `rtc_read_time` extracts the 12-hour-mode PM bit before BCD decoding and treats decoded hours >12 as 24-hour values (some RTCs report unreliable mode bits). All QEMU invocations (Makefile run targets and both integration harnesses) pass `-rtc base=utc` so the guest RTC reads UTC. `vbe_put_pixel` must bounds-check coordinates against `vbe_state.width`/`height` before computing the framebuffer address — an out-of-range cursor value once caused an intermittent kernel panic; dropped pixels are reported on serial as `[VBE] dropped out-of-bounds pixel`.
- `src/fs/`: FAT32 split into `fat32_core.c` (sector/cluster IO, FAT chains, mount), `fat32_name.c` (8.3/LFN/UTF-16 name codec), `fat32_dir.c` (directory entries, paths, mkdir/rmdir), and `fat32.c` (public file operations); shared internals live in `fat32_int.h` (`g_fs`, `g_sector`, `g_cluster`, cross-file prototypes).
- `src/lib/`: freestanding standard-library string and stdio routines.
- `mini-libc/`: MIT-licensed user-space C library for Ring 3 programs; every file carries `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`. Currently `include/sys/syscall.h` (ABI constants mirroring `include/os/syscall.h`: `SYS_*` classes, sub-ops, `SYSFS_O_*`, `PROC_STATE_*`), `syscall.S` (`syscall0`–`syscall3` cdecl wrappers marshalling args into `eax`=class/`ebx`=op/`ecx`/`edx`/`esi`, preserving callee-saved registers), `src/crt0.S` (the `_start` ELF entry point: fabricates `argc`/`argv`/`envp`, calls `main`, exits via `PROC_EXIT`), and freestanding C11 modules under `src/` with headers under `include/`: `string.c`/`ctype.c` (`string.h`/`ctype.h`), `stdio.c` (`stdio.h`/`stdarg.h` — console+string `printf`/`scanf` family plus unbuffered `FILE*` streams `stdin`/`stdout` and `fopen`/`fread`/`fprintf`/`fscanf`/etc. over `fs.h`), `errno.c` (`errno.h`), `time.c` (`time.h` — UTC+8 calendar/clock over `SYS_TIME`), `fs.c` (`fs.h` — FAT32 fd API plus a minimal `FILE`), `unistd.c` (`unistd.h`/`sys/types.h` — process/fd/path wrappers, `ENOSYS` for unsupported calls), and `stdlib.c` (`stdlib.h` — `malloc` family with a 16-byte header giving 8-byte alignment, C11-checked `aligned_alloc`,, `atexit`, `exit`/`_Exit`/`abort`, `strtol`/`strtoul`, `rand`/`srand`, `qsort`/`bsearch`, `abs`/`div`). Base headers `stdint.h`/`stddef.h`/`stdbool.h`/`limits.h`/`float.h` are also provided; `examples/hello.c` shows the link recipe. The root Makefile builds the library via `make libmyc` into `build/libmyc.a` (`LIBMYC_*` variables; objects under `$(BUILD_DIR)/mini-libc/`). **mini-libc development happens on the dedicated `mini-libc` branch** — commit mini-libc changes there directly instead of opening per-change feature branches; merge it into `main` at milestones or on request.
- `include/arch/x86/`, `include/mm/`, `include/os/`, `include/shell/`, `include/drivers/`, `include/fs/`, and `include/lib/`: public headers grouped with their subsystem. Keep `include/arch/x86/regs.h` synchronized with assembly stack frames; freestanding types and stdio/string interfaces live in `include/lib/`.
- `scripts/say_hi.py`: pull-request greeting script used by CI.
- `.github/workflows/pr_hi.yml`: runs the greeting script for pull requests.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`: builds the kernel and ISO for tagged releases or manual dispatch.
- `test/`: keep tests grouped by role: `python/` for discovered Python tests and source-contract checks (split by architecture, device, memory, ELF, and storage/shell); `c/` for host C test programs; `shell/` for one launcher per C suite; `support/` for the host-`cc` compile helper and C assertion header; and `integration/` for QEMU-only checks. Host C suites include PMM allocation/free checks above 4 GiB. The standard QEMU integration entry point is `run_qemu_integration.py`; `qemu_session.py`, `fat32_image.py`, `framework.py`, and scenario modules (`shell_scenarios.py`, `ring3_scenarios.py`, `page_fault_scenarios.py`) separate emulator control, test-disk setup, the unittest-style `QemuTestCase` base (`assertTrue`/`assertEqual`/`assertIn`/etc.; `test_*` methods run in sorted order alongside plain `check(session)` functions), and behavioral checks. `fault_demo.asm` is assembled five ways (`stack.elf`, `faultu.elf`, `faultp.elf`, `oom.elf`, `kfault.elf`) to exercise page-fault demand mapping, process termination, the out-of-memory kill, and the kernel-fault panic; `fs_demo.asm` (`fsdemo.elf`) exercises the filesystem syscalls and `PROC_EXIT`. The suite uses two QEMU sessions: the main session ends with `oom.elf` because leaked user-heap blocks exhaust the PMM, and a dedicated second session runs `kfault.elf` since the kernel panic reboots the machine. `run_qemu_highmem.py` is the separate bounded 6 GiB test for real high-frame allocation, mapping, data verification, and release. Run it explicitly via `make test-qemu-highmem`; the standard 128 MiB suite is `make test-qemu`, and both are separate from host-only `make test`.
- `README.md`: English user/build documentation rendered on the repo page; keep behavior and commands aligned. `README-zh.md` is its Chinese translation. `TODO.md` / `TODO-zh.md` stay at the root as the bilingual roadmap.
- `.github/agents/my-os-kernel.agent.md`: repository-specific agent instructions. Keep this file synchronized with repository changes.

## Architecture constraints

- Keep the kernel freestanding, 32-bit x86, and compatible with the existing C/NASM toolchain.
- IRQ0 and `int 0x80` frames must match `struct irq_frame` and their assembly push/pop order. Do not preempt arbitrary kernel syscall frames; use `PROC_YIELD` to switch at an explicit safe syscall boundary.
- Each Ring 3 process owns a private `struct user_mm` address space: a private PDPT[0]->PD chain for the low 1 GiB of user space, a private copy of the supervisor-only low 4 MiB identity map, and a shared PDPT[3] kernel half. CR3 is switched on every context switch; kernel code may run on any CR3 because the kernel half is identical. User pages below 4 MiB are refused; borrowed kernel pages (low identity map, `.user.text`) are marked with PTE bit 9 and never freed by `paging_mm_release`.
- Keep ELF user virtual ranges separate from linker-placed `.user.text`; ELF mappings belong to their scheduled process and must be released when it is killed.
- Update TSS `esp0` whenever switching the active user kernel stack. Avoid freeing a stack while it is still active.
- User mappings must remain below `USER_SPACE_END`; kernel mappings must not be made user-accessible.
- Hardware-facing changes need explicit bounds/format checks and must preserve serial diagnostics and fallback behavior. Planned networking and graphics/GUI work must preserve the VGA text-mode fallback and serial diagnostics; graphics code must keep the `vbe_put_pixel` bounds checks, and network drivers must degrade gracefully when no device is present (do not fail boot or block shell startup).
- ATA disk access is primary-master PIO/LBA28 only; FAT32 uses 512-byte sectors and supports ASCII LFN names (FAT32 limit: 255 UTF-16 code units); every Shell-created entry carries LFN entries that preserve the original case, lookups match the LFN case-sensitively, and only entries without LFN fall back to the uppercase 8.3 short name. Names that cannot fit 8.3 get generated `~N` aliases; keep the `needs_alias` flag separate from `lfn_entries`. Existing Shell path buffers impose a lower input limit. LFN directory entries must be sequence- and checksum-validated; convert UTF-16LE to ASCII with `?` for unsupported code units. Keep sector, cluster, name, and directory-slot bounds explicit and preserve partition/cluster zero checks.
- Disk Shell commands are `disk`, `ls`, `cat`, `write`, `cp`, `mv`, `rm`, `cd`, `mkdir`, `rmdir`, `run`, and `echo` (which writes to both the screen and the COM1 serial port); `cd` only changes into an existing directory, while `ls` defaults to the current directory and accepts an optional target path. `rmdir -f` recursively deletes files and subdirectories with a recursion bound and cannot delete the current directory or its parents. `cp` copies files and `cp -r` recursively copies directory trees; `mv` renames/moves files and directories. For `cp`, `cp -r`, and `mv`, an existing directory destination receives the source inside it (`dst`/`src-basename`), matching Linux semantics. `mv` replaces an existing destination file but refuses to replace a directory or move a directory into its own subtree; `cp -r` refuses to copy a directory into itself (checked via `fat32_path_within`). `fat32_list_directory` iterates a shared static cluster buffer, so its callback must not perform file I/O; collect entries first, then act on them. Keep command behavior and README summaries aligned.
- The FAT32 working directory (`g_cwd` in `src/fs/fat32.c`) is a normalized absolute path shared by the shell and user-mode `FS_CHDIR`/`FS_GETCWD`; `fat32_resolve_path` handles `.` and `..`. Show the path in the prompt only while FAT32 is mounted; otherwise keep the `myos >` prompt. User FS syscalls (`SYS_FS` ops 1–12) resolve paths through the same helper and validate user pointers against registered ranges; the fd table is global, not per-process. `SIG_KILL` (`SYS_SIG`/1) sends a signal and `SIG_SIGNAL` (`SYS_SIG`/2) sets a disposition; only `SIGINT`/`SIGKILL` are valid (`SIG_VALID`), and fatal unblocked signals kill via `ring3_signal_scan` on IRQ0 or the signal-aware `IO_READ`/`IO_GETCHAR` wait loops. Custom handlers are delivered by `sig_deliver()`: it copies the interrupted `irq_frame` into `sig_saved_frame`, writes a `[restorer][sig]` call frame on the user stack, and repoints `eip`/`useresp` at the handler. The restorer is a per-process user page at `USER_SIG_TRAMPOLINE` (0x00900000) running `mov eax,SYS_SIG; mov ebx,SIG_RETURN; int 0x80`; `SIG_RETURN` (`SYS_SIG`/3) restores the saved frame wholesale (registers included) and unblocks the signal. Only one handler level is tracked (`sig_active` defers further handled signals); delivering into a syscall frame abandons that syscall.
- `start_shell` polls the keyboard while waiting for input. Hide the prompt while a foreground Ring 3 process is selected, but continue accepting input so `bg`/`kill` can return control; restore the prompt when no foreground process remains. Do not replace this with a blocking `gets` while a foreground task may run, or its prompt/output will overlap and process control will stop responding.
- The keyboard driver maps arrow keys to the `KEYBOARD_KEY_UP`/`DOWN`/`LEFT`/`RIGHT` control bytes (0x01–0x04) and Ctrl+C to `KEYBOARD_KEY_SIGINT` (0x05), all of which also reach `IO_READ`/`IO_GETCHAR` consumers; the syscall wait loops convert a self-read 0x05 into SIGINT. When the keyboard buffer is empty and another Ring 3 process is runnable, `IO_READ`/`IO_GETCHAR` yield via `sys_keyboard_wait_yield`: it rewinds the saved frame's `eip` by 2 (`int 0x80` = `CD 80`) so the syscall restarts on resume, then switches through `syscall_switch_frame`. The shell keeps a 16-entry command history recalled with Up/Down and supports cursor-based line editing (Left/Right move an insertion point; printable keys insert there and Backspace deletes before it). All repaints go through `vga_set_cursor`/`vga_columns`, which delegate to VBE cell coordinates when VBE is active; editing keys are ignored while no prompt origin exists (foreground Ring 3 task). `split_line` groups non-empty double-quoted arguments (unterminated/empty/mid-word quotes stay literal, `\"` does not close a quote) and `shell_unescape_arg` expands `\n`, `\\`, and `\"` while warning on other escapes. Ctrl+C echoes `^C`, discards the line, signals the foreground process, and redraws the prompt.
- Kernel startup probes ATA and automatically calls the Shell `disk` initialization command only when a primary-master device is detected.
- Keep changes surgical; do not broaden a task into unrelated cleanup. Never hide an error behind a success-shaped fallback.

## Workflow

1. Read the affected implementation, header, assembly entry points, and callers before editing.
2. Search for existing helpers and tests before introducing new logic.
3. Make the smallest complete change and update directly related documentation.
4. Run `make test` for the host test suite and `make build` for kernel compilation when applicable. `make test` must be runnable without the cross-compiler; C suites must call host `cc`, and each case must print a useful name and PASS/FAIL status. Keep `src/kernel.c` as the top-level kernel file; place other C files and headers in matching `arch/x86`, `mm`, `os`, `drivers`, `fs`, or `lib` groups. Keep Python, C, shell-launcher, and QEMU integration files in their corresponding `test/` subdirectories; split static contracts by subsystem and keep the QEMU runner focused on orchestration. Privileged instructions and direct physical-memory paths should use stubs or source/layout checks rather than unsafe host execution. When runtime behavior is relevant and QEMU is installed, also run `make test-qemu`; the target has bounded waits and terminates its emulator.
5. Keep this agent guide synchronized with repository changes; update it in the same change whenever build/test behavior, architecture conventions, or file responsibilities change.
6. Branching: documentation-only changes may be committed directly on `main`. All other code changes must go on a dedicated branch named `feature/<topic>` (e.g. `feature/fat32-cp-mv-rename`), never directly on `main`.
7. Report changed files, exact validation results, and remaining hardware/emulation limitations. Do not claim a QEMU or hardware check that was not run.
